newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends see-saw day unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends see-saw day unchanged.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to off slightly near the close on Thursday, after gaining more than a half point in early trading.

Munis once again traced Treasury market volatility. The government long bond was up 2/32 at 98-12/32 heading into the New York close to yield 6.62 percent, after gaining more than a point in earlier trading.
"It's long overdue," one municipal trader said. "It's a long overdue correction we all were fighting, but that's what it looks like we've got."

Among actively traded secondary market bonds, bids on Cook County, Ill., FGIC 5-7/8s of 2022 were 1/8 higher at 99-3/4. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were one basis point lower at 5.67 percent.
Debt futures closed lower. The March municipal contract fell 10/32 to 114-24/32 and March T-bonds lost 13/32 to 112-16/32. The MOB spread widened to 72 ticks from 69 at the close on Wednesday.
In afternoon repricings, the Robinson-Humphrey Cos said it lowered yields on several maturities of Knox County Health Educational and Housing Facilities Board, Tenn.'s $84.6 million bond deal.

The largest deal of the day was a $307 million taxable pension bond issue from Alameda County, Calif. MR Beal & Co priced the 2018 maturity at a spread to Treasuries of 65 basis points. To see the final pricing, double click on nN12224181.

Friday's economic indicators include the University of Michigan report on December consumer sentiment at 1000 EST. A consensus survey of economists by Reuters showed expectations for a 99.2 reading, unchanged from November.
Despite the looming holidays, the new issue calendar for next week contains a healthy $2.45 billion in 91 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $731 million in 67 issues, with the largest a $130 million King County, Wash., sale on Monday.
Negotiated sales total $1.7 billion in 24 offerings. The largest is a $626 million New York City deal through Lehman Brothers.
